name: PouchDB
tagline: JavaScript database for browsers and Node that speaks the CouchDB replication protocol.
description: PouchDB is a JavaScript document database modelled on Apache CouchDB: it runs in the browser on IndexedDB, in Node on LevelDB, and replicates bidirectionally with CouchDB or any server that implements the CouchDB protocol. It pioneered the offline-first web app pattern and is still the simplest way to give a web app live sync with a CouchDB backend. Development is slow (the last major release was 9.0 in 2024, now under the Apache umbrella), and the revision-tree model it inherits from CouchDB makes storage grow unless you compact. Newer local-first libraries offer better TypeScript ergonomics and query power.

scale.notes: Bounded by browser storage quotas on the client; server-side scale comes from CouchDB.

strengths: Drop-in two-way replication with CouchDB and IBM Cloudant
Runs unchanged in browsers, Node.js, Electron and Cordova
Changes feed makes reactive UIs and background sync straightforward
Mature, battle-tested conflict model with deterministic winners
weaknesses: Revision history bloats storage unless you compact regularly
Mango queries are limited; no joins or aggregations
Slow release cadence and dated APIs compared with newer local-first libraries
useCases: Offline-capable web apps with a CouchDB backend
Field data collection that syncs when back online
notIdealFor: Large datasets beyond browser storage quotas
